name: clickables

operatingThreshold.rule: the lowest threshold whose precision on the out-of-fold predictions is at least 50% (with at least 5 elements flagged); if none reaches 50%, there is no threshold and no suggestions. The test websites are never used to choose it

selection.rule: the candidate with the highest out-of-fold PR-AUC in 5-fold cross-validation grouped by website on the development sites; the test sites are never used to choose
selection.reason: Highest out-of-fold PR-AUC (0.276) of the 1 candidates in 5-fold cross-validation grouped by website.

crossValidation.rule: the candidate with the highest out-of-fold PR-AUC in 5-fold cross-validation grouped by website on the development sites; the test sites are never used to choose

architecture: gradient-boosted trees over 92 features (300 trees, up to 15 leaves each), temperature-calibrated

data.note: Tranco top-1,000 crawl. Pages with document-level (delegated) click listeners are kept only when built with React, Vue or Angular; other delegated pages are dropped whole. Landmarks and page regions are not candidates. Training folds keep every positive and at most 10 negatives per positive. New labels were not hand-checked.

comparisons.model: Rule: pointer cursor and not native

beats_best_gbt.target: the graph network beats the best gradient-boosting baseline
beats_best_gbt.note: no graph network was trained in this run

latency.target: <= 50 ms for 2,000 elements in the Web Worker
latency.note: 10 runs in the app's Web Worker (median reported); Google Chrome 151.0.7922.137 (/opt/google/chrome/chrome), headless; CPU: 12th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-1255U, 12 logical cores; no CPU throttling

summary: The model is experimental and switched off by default. Its suggestions are advisory and never change the score, the history or the report.

Training data: the Tranco top-1,000 crawl. Pages with delegated (document-level) click listeners are kept only when they are built with React, Vue or Angular, which bind click handlers on each element where the labeller sees them; other delegated pages are dropped whole. The rule reads only page facts, never a label. The corpus has 178,314 candidate rows from 313 websites and 5,372 positives (55 of them from the 136 non-delegated websites the previous model used).
The labels on the newly added React, Vue and Angular pages come from the same automated probing and were NOT hand-checked; the earlier automated audit covered non-delegated pages only.

Only element-only gradient boosting was trained (the previous model's type). It was chosen and calibrated by 5-fold cross-validation grouped by website on 285 development websites (4,450 positives). Inside each training fold every positive was kept with at most 10 negatives per positive; validation folds and the held-out set were complete. Out-of-fold PR-AUC 0.276; temperature 0.621; threshold 0.906, the lowest with at least 50% out-of-fold precision.

Held-out set: 28 websites (23 React, 4 Vue, 1 Angular) drawn from the newly added websites before training and scored once: 31,951 elements, 922 positives. PR-AUC 0.408 (95% site-bootstrap interval 0.169-0.610), against 0.037 (0.026-0.066) for the previous model on the same set. At the threshold: 568 suggestions (17.8 per 1,000 elements), precision 53% (24-79%), recall 33% (13-53%). Precision is below the 90% the ship gate asks for, so the model stays off by default.
failurePatterns: The errors have not been reviewed by hand. errors.json holds a random 50 of the 266 false positives and 50 of the 620 false negatives on the held-out websites at the threshold. The sampled false positives cluster on a few websites (nike.com 12, tripadvisor.com 9, fontawesome.com 8) and include headings and wrappers with tabindex or menu-like classes. Some sampled misses look like ancestor-handler label noise (an empty outline wrapper, an image), which supports checking the new labels by hand.
limitations: The held-out websites are all delegated React, Vue or Angular websites, like most of the new training data, while the previous model was trained only on non-delegated pages. The comparison therefore shows the new model is much better on this kind of page; it does not show how either model does on other kinds of page.

Calibration error on the held-out set is 0.116, above the 0.05 gate (the previous model had 0.008 on its own, nearly all-negative test set). Negative sampling raises the share of positives the model sees in training, and temperature scaling only partly corrects it; read the confidence percentages as rough.

React supplies 4,530 of the 5,372 positives; Vue has 681 from 25 websites and Angular 106 from 3. The held-out set has 1 Angular website and 4 Vue websites, so the per-framework results are thin (Vue held-out PR-AUC 0.138 on 46 positives).
All examples come from the Tranco crawl, and the results are not representative of other kinds of websites. The previous run's 21 test websites are development websites in this run.

labelProbe.method: Random sample of labelled candidates; each clicked once at its centre in the live page. "responds": the DOM, address or a dialog changed within 400 ms. Skipped as untestable: pages that change by themselves, and elements whose centre is a link or button. A response can still come from a handler on an ancestor, so disagreement is an upper bound on label noise.

labelHandCheck.method: Method (ml/README.md, step 2): labels/sheet.mjs drew 300 random labelled elements; labels/audit.mjs re-checked each one in the live page with Chrome's DevTools Protocol, reading the element's own listeners and React handlers, its ancestors' and any document-level (delegated) listeners, and marked it correct, wrong or unsure; labels/score.mjs counted the verdicts. The check is automated: an independent manual review by the owner has not been done.
labelHandCheck.reading: This measures whether the labels are accurate on non-delegated pages, where it was run. It says nothing about the labels on the delegated React, Vue and Angular pages added in this run, which were not checked; only 4 of the judged labels were positive.
